prompt: Two series share the metric type `run.googleapis.com/request_count` but differ in `response_code_class`. How many series are they?
hint: Change any label and it is another series.

choices.text: One, with two values per point
choices.why: A point holds one value; the label makes a second series.

choices.text: Two
choices.why: Right. Each combination of labels is its own series.

choices.text: One, because the metric type is the same
choices.why: The type is one of three parts of the name, not the whole of it.

choices.text: None until a reducer combines them
choices.why: They exist as series before any reducer.

prompt: A process exports the total number of orders since it started. Which kind is that?
hint: It only grows, until a restart.

choices.text: GAUGE
choices.why: A gauge is a value at an instant, like memory in use.

choices.text: DELTA
choices.why: A delta is what happened in one interval only.

choices.text: CUMULATIVE
choices.why: Right. A total since a start time.

choices.text: DISTRIBUTION
choices.why: Distribution is a value type, a histogram, not a kind.

prompt: Which of these does the shop pay to send to Cloud Monitoring?
hint: Google's own metrics are free to receive.

choices.text: run.googleapis.com/request_count
choices.why: Google publishes it; it is non-chargeable.

choices.text: A custom metric its own code writes
choices.why: Right. Charged by the MiB received, after 150 free.

choices.text: The uptime check's results, as metrics
choices.why: The executions are charged, not the resulting metric.

choices.text: Instance counts of its Cloud Run revisions
choices.why: Also a Google metric, and free.

prompt: In minute 10 the counter grew by 624. What is `ALIGN_RATE` per second over the 60-second period?
hint: Delta divided by the period's seconds.

prompt: The mean latency is about 90 ms and the median 45 to 50 ms. What does the mean describe?
hint: Where did any request actually land?

choices.text: A typical request
choices.why: The typical request is the median, near 50 ms.

choices.text: The slow requests
choices.why: Those took 2,400 ms, the p99.

choices.text: No request: it sits between the fast and the slow
choices.why: Right. It is pulled both ways and lands where nobody was.

choices.text: The worst minute of the ten
choices.why: Each row has its own mean; none is the worst minute.

prompt: A two-minute outage happened yesterday, and the week's dashboard at a one-hour alignment period shows nothing. Why?
hint: What does one point per hour hold?

choices.text: Cloud Monitoring drops data older than a day
choices.why: The data is kept; it is summarised by the period.

choices.text: Two minutes were averaged into an hour
choices.why: Right. A one-minute period would show it.

choices.text: Outages are recorded only by uptime checks
choices.why: The request metrics recorded it too, at minute resolution.

choices.text: The reducer removed the failing revision
choices.why: A sum keeps every series' contribution.

prompt: Three instances report p99 latencies of 60, 70 and 2,000 ms. What is the service's p99?

choices.text: 710 ms, the mean of the three
choices.why: A mean of percentiles is not a percentile.

choices.text: 2,000 ms, the largest
choices.why: Only if that instance served most of the traffic.

choices.text: 70 ms, the middle one
choices.why: The median of three percentiles is not the service's either.

choices.text: It cannot be told from these three numbers
choices.why: Right. Combine the distributions first, then read the percentile.

prompt: Put the steps of the dashboard's first chart in the order Cloud Monitoring applies them.
hint: Per series first, across series last.
items: Align each series to a rate over 60 seconds
Sum the series in each group
trap: Summing before aligning is the slip: cumulative counters with different start times cannot be added.

prompt: The API process crashed and exports no metrics. Which of these still notices?

choices.text: The uptime check
choices.why: Right. It depends on nothing the process reports.

choices.text: A chart of the process's custom metrics
choices.why: A dead process writes nothing, so the chart just stops.

choices.text: The dashboard's p99 latency line
choices.why: No requests served means no latencies recorded.

choices.text: A reducer grouped by revision
choices.why: It can only combine series that exist.

prompt: The shop's `/healthz` is changed to query the database. The database becomes slow. What does the uptime check report?
hint: What is an uptime check for?

choices.text: Nothing: health checks ignore slow answers
choices.why: A slow answer past the timeout is a failure.

choices.text: A precise alert naming the database
choices.why: It names the URL; it knows nothing of the database.

choices.text: The site down, from every region at once
choices.why: Right. Which is why /healthz checks only the process.

choices.text: A warning only from the region nearest the database
choices.why: Every region asks the same URL and sees the same slowness.

prompt: An uptime check runs every 5 minutes from 3 regions. How many executions is that in a 730-hour month?
hint: Regions times runs per hour times hours.

prompt: In the dashboard JSON, the aligner that divides each interval's growth by its seconds is `ALIGN____`.
Which of these did the lesson run on your computer? Choose all that apply.
hint: Arithmetic and plans, yes; Google's service, no.

choices.text: The aligners' arithmetic on generated data
choices.why: Yes, align.py.

choices.text: Terraform's plan of an uptime check
choices.why: Yes, computed locally.

choices.text: An uptime check asking the shop from three regions
choices.why: No. Nothing executes checks locally.

choices.text: A dashboard drawn by Cloud Monitoring
choices.why: No. Only its JSON was planned.

prompt: Latency alerts look at p99 over several minutes rather than one point. Which row of align.py's output shows why?
hint: One minute looks healthy and is not different.

choices.text: Minute 1, where the mean is highest
choices.why: A high mean is not the lesson about single points.

choices.text: Minute 5, where p99 drops to 55 by chance
choices.why: Right. One quiet minute would reset a one-point alert.

choices.text: Minute 4, the busiest
choices.why: Traffic level does not change the percentile story here.

choices.text: Minute 10, the last one
choices.why: Nothing about it differs from the others.
